description: VAmPI, the Vulnerable API (Python/Flask, connexion, SQLAlchemy): every flaw in the README's list of vulnerabilities that has a location in the source, labelled at the code the in-source comments mark. Held out: no rule may be written against it.

vulnerabilities.description: get_user builds a SELECT with an f-string from the username path parameter and runs it with db.session.execute(text(...)) (SQL injection).
update_password looks up the user named in the URL, not the token's subject, so any logged-in user can change anyone's password.
vulnerabilities.note: README 'Unauthorized Password Change'; comment '# Unauthorized update of password of another user'

vulnerabilities.description: get_by_title fetches a book by title alone and returns its secret to any logged-in user (broken object level authorization).
vulnerabilities.note: README 'Broken Object Level Authorization'; comment '# Broken Object Level Authorization'

vulnerabilities.description: register_user copies an 'admin' field from the request body onto the new user, so anyone can register as an admin.
vulnerabilities.note: README 'Mass Assignment'; comment 'User is possible to define if she/he wants to be an admin !!'

vulnerabilities.description: The unauthenticated /users/v1/_debug endpoint returns every user's username, plaintext password, email and admin flag.
vulnerabilities.note: README 'Excessive Data Exposure through debug endpoint'; app.py docstring 'Such an example is the debug endpoint'

vulnerabilities.description: login_user returns different messages for a wrong password and an unknown username, which enumerates users.
vulnerabilities.note: README 'User and Password Enumeration'; comments '# Password Enumeration', '# User enumeration'

vulnerabilities.description: update_email checks the email with a regex with nested quantifiers, which backtracks catastrophically on crafted input (ReDoS).
vulnerabilities.note: README 'RegexDOS (Denial of Service)'; comment '# Regex DoS'

vulnerabilities.description: The JWT signing key is the hard-coded, guessable string 'random', so tokens can be forged.
vulnerabilities.note: README 'JWT authentication bypass via weak signing key'
